content: Extracellular fluid (ECF) refers to all the body fluids that exist outside the cells. The fluid that remains within the cells is referred to as intracellular fluid. In certain animals, including mammals, the extracellular fluid is further categorized into two primary subcompartments: interstitial fluid (ISF) and blood plasma. Blood plasma constitutes approximately 5% of the extracellular fluid. In humans, the concentration of glucose in the extracellular fluid is tightly regulated by homeostatic mechanisms and is typically around 5 millimolar (mM).
